chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is nothing prescribed (in particular) from the supplications of the evening of Arafah.
ai.seo_question: Is there a specific prescribed supplication for the evening of Arafah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the evening of Arafah is a time of open divine grace where any sincere supplication is accepted, rather than being restricted to a specific prescribed text. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the accessibility of personal du'a during the peak of Hajj rituals, distinguishing it from obligatory ritual prayers. The narration underscores the spiritual flexibility and generosity of Allah towards pilgrims on this significant day.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Salih Bin Abu Al Aswad, from Abu Al Jaroud, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is nothing from the supplications of the evening of Arafaat, anything Prescribed (in particular).
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Salih ibn abu al-Aswad from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
There is no definite prayer and supplication for the evening of the day of ‘Arafah.’” (Hadith 6 of this Chapter is best explained by Fatwa)
